## Summary

R caches the contents of lazy-load databases (`.rdb` files) in memory, keyed
by file path alone, with no invalidation (`readRawFromFile()` in
`src/main/serialize.c`). `unloadNamespace()` flushes only the package's
*code* database (`R/<pkg>.rdb`) from this cache. The package's other
lazy-load databases -- `help/<pkg>.rdb`, `R/sysdata.rdb`, and
`data/Rdata.rdb` -- are never flushed.

As a result, when a package is unloaded, re-installed, and re-loaded within
a single R session, offsets from the freshly-read `.rdx` index are applied
to a stale cached copy of the corresponding `.rdb` file. This produces two
distinct failure modes:

1. **Help pages**: queries fail until the session is restarted, with

   ```
   Error in fetch(key) :
     lazy-load database '.../help/<pkg>.rdb' is corrupt
   In addition: Warning message:
   internal error ... in R_decompress1
   ```

2. **Lazy data (silent)**: when a blob's offset happens to coincide across
   the two installations, a stale `data/Rdata.rdb` silently serves values
   from the *previously installed version* of the package, with no error or
   warning. (`R/sysdata.rdb` behaves the same way, by the same mechanism.)

The first failure mode is a long-standing source of "restart R" advice and
downstream bug reports. Package managers that can re-install packages
in-session work around it by calling the internal `lazyLoadDBflush()`
themselves from `.onUnload()` -- see e.g. renv
(<https://github.com/rstudio/renv/issues/1294>) and pak -- which requires
contortions to keep `R CMD check` quiet about the `.Internal()` call in
package code.

The second failure mode appears not to have been reported before, and is
arguably worse: silently wrong data rather than an error.

## Reproduction

Run in a fresh session (tested on macOS arm64 and Linux; platform-independent):

```
lib <- tempfile("lib"); dir.create(lib)
.libPaths(c(lib, .libPaths()))
src <- tempfile("src"); dir.create(src)
pkg <- file.path(src, "lazytest")
dir.create(file.path(pkg, "R"), recursive = TRUE)
dir.create(file.path(pkg, "man"), recursive = TRUE)
dir.create(file.path(pkg, "data"), recursive = TRUE)

writeLines(c("Package: lazytest", "Version: 1.0", "Title: Test",
             "Description: Test.", "Author: A", "Maintainer: A <a@b.c>",
             "License: GPL-3", "LazyData: true"),
           file.path(pkg, "DESCRIPTION"))
writeLines("export(f)", file.path(pkg, "NAMESPACE"))
writeLines("f <- function() 42", file.path(pkg, "R", "f.R"))

rd <- function(x)
  writeLines(c("\\name{f}", "\\alias{f}", "\\title{t}", "\\description{d}",
               paste0("\\details{", x, "}")),
             file.path(pkg, "man", "f.Rd"))
mkdata <- function(x) {
  d <- x
  save(d, file = file.path(pkg, "data", "d.rda"))
}

rd("short docs"); mkdata("short")
install.packages(pkg, lib = lib, repos = NULL, type = "source")
library(lazytest)
length(tools::Rd_db("lazytest", lib.loc = lib))  # ok; populates help cache
lazytest::d                                      # "short"; populates data
cache

detach("package:lazytest", character.only = TRUE)
unloadNamespace("lazytest")

rd(strrep("much longer docs to shift the offsets ", 50))
```

```
Note the final result: the old version's data value is returned silently,

## Proposed patch

`unloadNamespace()` already flushes `R/<pkg>.rdb`, precisely so that the
unload + re-install + re-load cycle works for package code. The attached
patch (against trunk) extends the same treatment to the package's other
lazy-load databases:

```
Index: src/library/base/R/namespace.R
===================================================================
--- src/library/base/R/namespace.R      (revision 90386)
+++ src/library/base/R/namespace.R      (working copy)
@@ -907,7 +907,13 @@ unloadNamespace <- function(ns)
        .Internal(unregisterNamespace(nsname))
        if(.isMethodsDispatchOn() && methods:::.hasS4MetaData(ns))
            methods::cacheMetaData(ns, FALSE, ns)
+       ## flush the package's lazy-load databases: stale cached copies
+       ## could otherwise be seen if the package is re-installed and
+       ## re-loaded in this session
        .Internal(lazyLoadDBflush(paste0(nspath, "/R/", nsname, ".rdb")))
+       .Internal(lazyLoadDBflush(paste0(nspath, "/R/sysdata.rdb")))
+       .Internal(lazyLoadDBflush(paste0(nspath, "/data/Rdata.rdb")))
+       .Internal(lazyLoadDBflush(paste0(nspath, "/help/", nsname, ".rdb")))
     }
     invisible()
 }
```

Flushing a path with no cache entry (e.g. for packages without help or
lazy data) is a no-op: `do_lazyLoadDBflush()` only searches the in-memory
name table and never touches the filesystem. The cost is a bounded string
comparison per database per unload; eviction also releases up to 10Mb of
cached contents per database.

With this patch applied, both the help query and the data access in the
reproduction above return the newly installed version's contents.

The patch is also available as a pull request on the r-svn CI mirror, with
builds and checks run on Linux, macOS, and Windows:
<https://github.com/r-devel/r-svn/pull/295> (diff:
<https://github.com/r-devel/r-svn/pull/295.diff>)

## Notes on scope

- The cache is keyed by the literal path string. This patch flushes the
  namespace's stored (normalized) path, which matches how the help and
  data cache keys are constructed in standard use, since `.libPaths()`
  entries are normalized. Loading a package from an unnormalized `lib.loc`
  spelling not on `.libPaths()` can still defeat the flush; that
  limitation applies identically to the existing `R/<pkg>.rdb` flush
  (`loadNamespace()` keys its lazy-load promises with the raw
  `find.package()` path, while `unloadNamespace()` flushes the normalized
  stored path), so it is not made worse here.

- Re-installation performed by another process (a second R session, or
  `R CMD INSTALL` from a terminal) while the package's databases are
  cached is still not covered. A complete fix would validate cache
  entries inside `readRawFromFile()` against the file's current
  size/mtime/inode, invalidating stale entries at fetch time regardless
  of how or where the re-installation happened. I am happy to propose
  that patch instead of (or in addition to) this one.

- Related observation while reading `readRawFromFile()`: on a cache hit,
  the code performs `memcpy(RAW(val), ptr[icache]+offset, len)` without
  storing or checking the cached file's length, so index offsets pointing
  beyond the end of a stale (smaller) cached file read out of bounds of
  the malloc'd buffer. Validating entries at fetch time (previous bullet)
  would remove that possibility; alternatively a bounds check could be
  added cheaply by recording each cached file's length.
```
